page.overview:
What is Snaga?

Snaga was a contemptuous term that was used in the Third Age for the lowest or lesser breeds of the Orcs of Mordor and Isengard. The term was used most especially among the larger and stronger Uruk-hai.

In the year 3019, there was an Orc addressed as Snaga in the band of Isengarders led by Uglúk tasked to pursue the Fellowship of the Ring. After the band captured Meriadoc Brandybuck and Peregrin Took, two of the four hobbits, they were tasked with returning with them to Saruman. When Uglúk believed that the Rohirrim had been made aware of them, Snaga was blamed for it and the Uruk-hai captain then threatened that he would cut off his ears. Snaga was killed with the rest of the Orc-band on February 29 by Éomer's éored.

One of the Mordor-orcs in the Tower of Cirith Ungol under Shagrat's command was addressed as Snaga. He was his only surviving subordinate after the Quarrel with Gorbag's company from Minas Morgul. He met Samwise Gamgee on the stairs of the tower before running off to the higher levels. However, he then got in the way of Shagrat, whom he had betrayed. The Uruk captain began to threaten that he would either be fed to Shelob or killed in a similar manner to Radbug. Snaga mockingly told him that all of his loyal soldiers had been killed by the "Morgul-rats" led by Gorbag. Shagrat attempted to kill the lesser Orc, who evaded him and climbed the stairs to the Look-out Room beneath the Upper Chamber where the captive Frodo Baggins was. Snaga then used a ladder to enter the Upper Chamber

Snaga is a word in the Black Speech meaning "slave" Coincidentally, Snaga means "strength" in many Slavic languages, including Serbian, Croatian, and Bosnian.
